title: Fiddler on the Roof
tagline: One dairyman, five daughters, and enough blintzes to go round.
about: In a small Jewish village in Tsarist Russia in 1905, a poor dairyman tries to hold on to the old ways as his three eldest daughters choose their own husbands.
cue: Serve the challah when Golde lights the candles for the Friday night dinner.

Tevye's KitchenFiddler on the RoofOne dairyman, five daughters, and enough blintzes to go round.Every recipe serves 4.
    StartersMainsSweetsDrinks
    StartersGolde's Friday night challahSoft plaited egg bread sweetened with honey, glazed golden and scattered with sesame seedsHow to make it7g dried yeast3 tbsp honey200ml warm water500g bread flour1 1/2 tsp salt2 eggs1 egg yolk, for glazing60ml vegetable oil1 tbsp sesame seedsStir the yeast and honey into the warm water and leave until foamy.Add the flour, salt, eggs and oil and knead for 10 minutes until smooth and springy.Cover and prove until doubled.Divide into 3, roll each into a 40cm rope and plait them, tucking the ends under.Set on a lined tray, cover loosely and prove until puffy. Heat the oven to 190°C.Brush with the egg yolk, scatter with sesame seeds and bake until deep golden and hollow when tapped underneath.Cool on a rack before tearing.Yente's chopped herring on ryePickled herring chopped by hand with egg, apple and red onion, spread thick on dark rye with dillHow to make it2 eggs300g pickled herring fillets, drained1 green apple, peeled and cored1/2 small red onion1 tbsp white vinegar1 tsp caster sugarblack pepper, to taste8 slices of dark rye bread1 tbsp dill, choppedBoil the eggs for 10 minutes, then cool in cold water and peel.Chop the herring, eggs, apple and onion finely by hand on a board.Mix with the vinegar, sugar and plenty of black pepper.Cover and chill so the flavours settle.Spread thickly on the rye bread and scatter with dill.MainsTevye's dairyman cheese blintzesThin pancakes rolled around sweet lemon and vanilla cheese, fried golden in butter, with sour cream and warm cherriesHow to make it150g plain flour3 eggs375ml milkpinch of salt30g butter, melted, for the batter400g ricotta150g cream cheese, softened1 egg yolk2 tbsp caster sugar, for the filling1 tsp vanilla extract1 lemon, zested and juiced400g frozen pitted cherries3 tbsp caster sugar, for the cherries2 tsp cornflour40g butter, for frying200g sour creamWhisk the flour, eggs, milk, salt and melted butter to a smooth thin batter and rest it.Beat the ricotta, cream cheese, egg yolk, filling sugar, vanilla and lemon zest until smooth.Simmer the cherries with their sugar and the lemon juice until juicy, then stir in the cornflour mixed with a splash of water and bubble until glossy.Cook 12 thin pancakes in a lightly buttered 20cm frying pan, on one side only, and stack them cooked side up.Put a heaped spoonful of filling on each, fold in the sides and roll into a parcel.Fry the parcels in the frying butter, seam side down first, until golden on both sides.Serve 3 each with sour cream and the warm cherries.Golde's potato kugelCrisp-edged potato and onion bake. Tradition!How to make it1.2kg floury potatoes1 brown onion3 eggs40g matzo meal80ml vegetable oilPour half the oil into a baking tin and heat it in the oven at 200°C.Grate the potatoes and onion, then squeeze out as much liquid as you can in a clean tea towel.Mix with the eggs, matzo meal, the rest of the oil, plenty of salt and pepper.Spread into the hot tin and bake until deep golden with crisp edges.SweetsGrandma Tzeitel's honey cakeDark, moist honey cake spiced with cinnamon, clove, ginger and orange, topped with toasted almondsHow to make it3 eggs150g brown sugar250g honey125ml vegetable oil180ml strong black tea, cooled300g plain flour2 tsp baking powder1 tsp bicarbonate of soda2 tsp ground cinnamon1/2 tsp ground cloves1/2 tsp ground ginger1 orange, zested50g flaked almondsHeat the oven to 170°C and line a 23cm square cake tin.Whisk the eggs and brown sugar until thick, then whisk in the honey, oil and tea.Whisk in the flour, baking powder, bicarbonate of soda, spices and orange zest to a smooth, runny batter.Pour into the tin, scatter with the almonds and bake until dark and springy and a skewer comes out clean.Cool in the tin before cutting into squares.DrinksSamovar glass tea with lemon and cherry jamStrong black tea poured into glasses with a slice of lemon, cherry jam and sugar cubes on the sideHow to make it2 tbsp strong loose leaf black tea1 L boiling water1 lemon, thinly sliced4 tbsp cherry jam8 sugar cubesBrew the tea in a small pot with 250ml of the boiling water for 5 minutes to make a strong concentrate.Pour a little concentrate into 4 heatproof glasses and top up with the rest of the boiling water to taste.Serve each glass with a lemon slice, a spoonful of cherry jam and sugar cubes on the side.Slivovitz plum brandyL'chaim. Tevye and Lazar Wolf shake on it.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
